title: Kickerboard: quant bug harvest & onboarding notes — week of 2026-05-21
content:
Purpose: quick harvest of small but recurrent quantization and onboarding issues observed this sprint. Focus areas: 1) 8-bit group quant artifacts, 2) KV-cache misalignment during prefix-caching experiments, 3) small-eval regressions in sampling quality on long prompts. Use this as the working log for the week; TODOs and owners at the bottom.

Attendees (sync): Avery, Maya, Diego, Ruth, Samir (quick async notes gathered from thread #applied-ml-quant and today's 30m sync).

Summary of what we saw this week
- Symptom A (intermittent): decoded outputs on long-context (1k+ tokens) have abrupt topical drift after a repeat token window when using 4-bit/8-bit hybrid quant with group size=128 on the L2-onboarded model. Appears only when continuous batching is enabled with batch size > 8.
  - Repro steps: see PR link. Repro is flaky locally but reliably reproduced on dedicated-staging with load test config "microburst-3x".
  - Immediate hypothesis: group quant bucket boundaries + packed attention kernel rounding leads to small fp accumulation that shifts rotary embedding phase over long sequences.

- Symptom B (KV-cache mismatch): canary rollout of the compact-quant variant produced off-by-one token repeat for long prefix-cached calls when fallback to float path occurred mid-request (fallback due to OOM on one GPU).
  - Root cause suspected: cache index mapping uses per-shard token offset derived from batch-shape inference that differs between quant and float paths. We saw mismatch logs: cache_index_map sizes differ by 1-2 for certain length buckets.

- Symptom C (eval regressions): small but measurable decrease in coherence metric (n-gram overlap and human-rated fluency) on the 'multi-turn summarization' eval set after quantization with per-channel scale (pcq) calibration using minmax calibration with tiny-calib set. Perplexity rise +2.1% on average; sampling metrics degrade for temperature>0.7.

Quick experiments run and results
- Per-layer calibration vs global: ran per-layer minmax and per-channel EMQ on 4 random checkpoints. Per-channel EMQ consistently reduced perplexity penalty (avg -0.9% vs minmax), but added ~5% CPU overhead in preprocess for calibration.
- Group size sweep: tested group_size in {64,128,256} on 4-bit weight quant; found group=64 reduced drift but increased model size slightly (metadata overhead) and slowed inference kernels ~3%. Narrowed to 64 as temporary safety mode for long-context endpoints.
- Fallback path instrumentation: added signals to log per-request cache_index_map and fallback_reason on staging. Found ~14 occurrences in 24h where fallback triggered due to transient memory pressure during autoscaling.
- Sampling eval: added nucleus sampling stability test (5 seeds) — quantized model fails 2/5 seeds where baseline passes; failure pattern is lower repetitiveness penalty handling in the logits correction path.

Actionable mitigations (short term)
1) Safety switch for long-context endpoints: pin group_size=64 and enable "rotary-phase-stabilizer" shim (lightweight phase correction applied to cached rotary embeddings) for dedicated-staging and canary routes. Owner: Diego. ETA: 48h.
2) Cache index mapping hardening: align mapping computation to use absolute-token-offset (global) instead of batch-relative offsets; add cross-check assertion that cache_index_map lengths match between quant/float route before merge. Owner: Samir. ETA: 72h.
3) Calibration change: adopt per-channel EMQ calibration for all model onboardings that will serve >512 token contexts; add a slower but more robust path to the onboarding pipeline. Owner: Maya + infra help from Ruth. ETA: next onboarding run.
4) Autoscaler tweak: add soft-margin memory pad to avoid mid-request fallbacks (configurable per machine type). Owner: infra-team ticket (see linked PR). ETA: next infra deploy.

Longer-term questions / experiments to prioritize
- Is rotary-phase drift a quant artifact only for certain kernel fusion strategies? Need controlled experiment: quant + unfused attention vs quant + fused attention across group sizes and rotary embedding implementations. (Diego + Avery)
- Can we design a cheap per-request calibration sanity check that detects and refuses to serve when predicted drift exceeds threshold? This would prevent bad outputs but cost latency on failed checks. (Maya)
- Explore mixed-precision KV-cache: store activations in 16-bit even if weights are 4-bit to reduce accumulation error for very long contexts. Measure memory impact vs quality. (Ruth)

Notes to self / messy capture (tacit context)
- Many of these issues are subtle and show up only under continuous batching + prefix cache + long prompts. Locally we rarely hit because our tests are short. Need to expand long-tail sampling harness in CI.
- The tiny-calib set used by onboarding was biased towards short dialogues; update to include at least 20% long-form docs and 10% adversarial numerical sequences.
- Conversation with infra: heartbeat OOMs are often because burst-scaler allocates smaller instance types first; request a new instance class with slightly higher memory headroom for compact-quant routes.

Meeting artifacts and references
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/8123 (instrumentation + rotary stabilizer prototype)
- JIRA: AM-4567 (compact-quant canary failures)
- Confluence sketch: applied-ml/compact-quant-hypothesis-notes (internal doc id in linked_artifacts)

Open TODOs (short list)
- [ ] Diego: push rotary-phase-stabilizer to staging and run 10k-token soak. (ETA 48h)
- [ ] Samir: add assertion and unit-test for cache_index_map length parity. (ETA 72h)
- [ ] Maya & Ruth: update onboarding calibration to EMQ per-channel, schedule re-onboard run for the L2 checkpoint. (ETA next onboard)
- [ ] Avery: add 3 long-context scenarios to CI sampling suite; add seeds for nucleus sampling stability. (ETA next sprint)
- [ ] Team: decide whether to default to group_size=64 for all long-context models. (Discuss in Friday sync)

Retro / what went well
- Good visibility: the instrumentation we shipped last sprint made triage far faster — found 14 fallbacks in logs within an hour.
- Rapid experiments: per-layer calibration test quickly identified EMQ benefit — good win.

Quick calendar notes
- Friday 2026-05-28: deep-dive on rotary/quant artifacts (60m). Invite: eng-applied-ml, infra-rep, serving-runtime eng.

If anything is urgent ping #applied-ml-quant or DM me (Avery). This doc is the working log for the week; will prune and append after Friday sync and convert to a short summary for the product onboarding channel.

-- end --
